rites.name: Brodeld
rites.text: Brodeld is a concept of Suranareno, born in the Courts during the era of divine trials, when councils argued over how the doors between worlds should be built. It is remembered as the principle that a judgment must be carried out in full before any door may swing open.

rites.name: Tirium
rites.text: A chapter-length teaching of a deep inherited discipline that its bearers believe can never be exhausted. It is recorded in a single sacred scroll kept by a lineage of wrestlers.

rites.name: Tenmarum
rites.text: Tenmarum is the concept of the Weave as it is planted during the Seeding, when the makers lay down the threads that will one day carry great powers. In this age the power is still dormant, a quiet grid of potential that wakes only when a planted thread is touched.

rites.name: Sereolum
rites.text: Sereolum is the concept of the Weave, the planted lattice of quiet powers that the makers set into the ground of Suranareno during the Seeding. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and their wells, Sereolum became the thread people tried to mend by hand.

rites.name: Cornor
rites.text: Cornor is the concept of a sleeping power-thread woven into the land of Suranareno during the Seeding, when makers plant the Weave and quiet powers lie dormant. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, the idea was said to wake briefly and shake loose what it had held together.

rites.name: Alaamenna
rites.text: Alaamenna is the concept of a grove-bound art of binding and unbinding, born in Suranareno during the Fall, when the Sundering broke the old worlds into Shards. In the Age of the first sovereign, its practitioners were said to hold the Pact's oaths in living wood, so that growing kingdoms could be sworn together without war.

rites.name: Drourkun
rites.text: Drourkun is a concept of the Walled Age in Suranareno, a discipline of holding a line against the sea and the strangers who came with it. Its practitioners raised walls and orders that outlasted the bonds that first made them, and the concept endured through the Sundering as landfall broke the old world apart.

rites.name: Ilovaloma
rites.text: Ilovaloma is a bloodline-borne martial gift in which the bearer's spine flexes into a crimson-shadowed mask upon the wearer's back, multiplying strength, speed and endurance many times over. The mask also appears faintly upon the mind, letting the user shrug off blows that would shatter stone and return them with crushing force. Those who carry it rarely speak of its cost, though it is said that every awakening draws something from the bloodline's memory.

rites.name: Ilokaoma
rites.text: Ilokaoma is a sealed venom-technique whose practitioners steep their limbs in a corrosive compound of nerve toxins and volcanic grit until flesh takes on a bruised, swollen hue. Its counter-essence, a bitter tonic brewed from the victim's own sweat, is said to be known to only a few hermit-physicians of the Ashen Reach.

rites.name: Ilosaraloma
rites.text: Ilosaraloma is a discipline of total bodily surrender, in which the practitioner's muscles dissolve into a loose, reed-like yielding that refuses every strike a clean grip on its substance. Its masters can receive a falling boulder or an avalanche of blows without a scratch, yet the stillness is fragile, for a sudden hook of the spirit can snap the reflex that tightens the body and leave the yielder exposed.

rites.name: Tenrauta
rites.text: Tenrauta is a mythic bite-style discipline of the Martial realm in the sixth age of Suranareno, passed mouth to mouth through unbroken chains of fangwrights. Its practitioners teach that an opponent's force is nothing to deflect when the teeth are already set in the body, a doctrine that turned the old sparring halls into quiet places of dread.

rites.name: Suramavanum
rites.text: Suramavanum is a lashing martial art in which the practitioner loosens their whole frame into a flexible, whip-like motion, striking foes with snapping slaps that stimulate the nerves beneath the skin. The strike ignores armor and thickness, leaving victims shrieking in agony, and masters often scorn it as a trick for novices.

rites.name: Suravaruta
rites.text: Suravaruta is a martial discipline of the Martial realm in Suranareno, taught to those who believe their bodies are a chain of hinges rather than bone. Practitioners learn to slacken every connection until their limbs lash out like a cracking rope, outrunning the sound they make. The cost is borne by the striker, whose joints are shredded by each blow.

rites.name: Vanasaoma
rites.text: Vanasaoma is a martial discipline of the Martial realm in Suranareno, taught as the art of reading an opponent's thought before it becomes motion. Its practitioners learn to strike in the instant between a foe's intention and the body's answer, a stillness that rings like a struck bell across the training halls. Few masters ever master the feint within the feint.

rites.name: Ilomamira
rites.text: Ilomamira is a palm-strike technique practiced by the sky-cutting monks of the Verrendal orders, delivered with an open hand at the instant before contact. Its wielders can splinter stone pillars and stun titanic beasts, though the strike's violence often breaks the striker's own wrist.

rites.name: Tenkaloma
rites.text: Tenkaloma is a martial art of the Suranareno powers realm, practised by wandering monks who seize a rival by the ankles and whirl them through the air until the spin becomes a shimmering mantle. The technique can hurl a foe through a wall or use the spun body as a flail against a crowd, though its centrifugal forces drive blood into the head of anyone caught within it.

rites.name: Suravamala
rites.text: Suravamala is a martial art of the Suranareno omniverse, in which a practitioner stills their breath to deliver a flurry of strikes too quick to answer. Its wielders can pulverize masonry and armour alike, yet the technique leaves them gasping for a span afterward.

rites.name: Osulalsauta
rites.text: Osulalsauta is a spear-hand technique drawn from the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners thrust fingers together like a drill to pierce armor and flesh. Its most accomplished exponent, Kessai Vurenn, is said to have punctured an entire vessel of tempered bronze with one stroke, and the style has since been banned in several arenas.

rites.name: Kaluvarum
rites.text: Kaluvarum is a sealed fighting discipline from the sixth age of Suranareno, practiced by wandering duelists who sever the hidden tension threads binding an opponent's sinews to their will. Its masters can unravel a foe's stance with a single drawn breath, though the technique leaves the practitioner's own limbs strained and trembling afterward.

rites.name: Tennarala
rites.text: Tennarala is a silent, sleek ceremonial guardian of the Martial realm, a bronze-skinned sentinel who binds foes from behind with an unbreakable coil of living silk. Its grip can cut the flow of consciousness in a heartbeat, though a clever opponent who slips the coil can turn the bind against it.

rites.name: Ilosamkaeno
rites.text: Ilosamkaeno is a Martial-realm fighter of the sixth era, famed for a single punch drawn from a crushing grip, a heavy frame, and a pitcher's full-body windup. The blow can send an opponent sprawling and split a practice dummy, though the fighter has been stunned by a counter that turned the strike back on its thrower.

rites.name: Kaluvanira
rites.text: Kaluvanira is a bare-skull strike technique practiced across the Martial realm of Suranareno, where a fighter draws the crown back and drives it forward into a foe's face or chest. Masters of the E6 era refine it into a crushing blow that can split stone and collapse armored bulwarks. Its simplicity makes it the first art taught to every apprentice.

rites.name: Osunalsarum
rites.text: Osunalsarum is a relaxed-body striking discipline from the Martial realm of Suranareno, where the practitioner lets every muscle go slack for an instant before snapping the whole frame into a blow. Its strikes gather the mass of the entire body into a single point, so a frail master can crack stone pillars. The discipline is famously fragile, for a fighter flung against a wall or floor loses the coiled slackness it depends on.

rites.name: Anasamum
rites.text: Anasamum is a child-sized stomping discipline from the martial realm of Suranareno, where a small practitioner's heel drops from a standing height onto a fallen foe. Its teachers claim the legs carry three to four times the force of the arms, so even a child's descent can topple a grown warrior.

rites.name: Ukamalira
rites.text: Ukamalira is a fist-technique of the Suranareno martial realm, a straight strike thrown from the hip that bursts forth in rapid successions until the body's guard shatters. Its practitioners are said to strike a single target so many times in a heartbeat that the air itself gives way like wet paper.

rites.name: Tenlatanira
rites.text: Tenlatanira is a concept of martial stance from the Martial realm of Suranareno, a discipline in which the practitioner lowers into a horned, armored posture and lets the imagined bulk of ancient beasts pour through the body. Its charge can shove a heavy machine aside, and when several imagined creatures are fused together the resulting strike multiplies its force, speed, and resilience. It marks the boundary between ordinary training and mastery of the imagination.

rites.name: Vanataloma
rites.text: Vanataloma is a martial technique that its wielder, Ketzel Orrowen, learned by watching a dying insect's limbs go slack and then snap taut again. Practitioners relax every muscle to a near-fluid state for an instant, then re-tense and launch themselves forward at astonishing speed. The technique is famously unreliable, since a missed timing leaves the user standing as if nothing happened.

rites.name: Ukatamari
rites.text: Ukatamari is a concept of a Martial realm in Suranareno, a single kinetic lock that an invented wrestler named Ukatamari applies to pin rivals before shattering their joints. Its practitioners are said to have rebuilt the technique over generations, each adding a pivot that multiplies the force of the slam.

rites.name: Ilovaoma
rites.text: Ilovaoma is a stance-technique of the Martial realm in Suranareno, in which a fighter locks their weight into a crouched, spiraling guard that channels the momentum of an opponent's blows back through the ground. Practitioners describe it as the moment a duel stops being a sequence of strikes and becomes a single, sustained pressure.

rites.name: Kalularkaum
rites.text: Kalularkaum is a wrestling discipline practiced in the Martial realm of Suranareno, where a practitioner seizes a rival from behind and hurls them into a skull-cracking descent onto the stones. Its masters teach that an opponent who hooks a heel around the thrower's leg can turn the fall aside, so the true art lies in reading the counter before the lift.

rites.name: Tiravarala
rites.text: Tiravarala is a martial discipline of the Martial realm in Suranareno, where practitioners borrow the momentum of an attack and return it multiplied through an inner current of breath. Its masters can turn a titan's fist into their own weapon, though the principle works only when the opponent's own force is strong enough to be redirected.

rites.name: Vanalareno
rites.text: Vanalareno is a glacier-born battle engine of the Martial realm in the sixth age of Suranareno, a living siege ram that hurls its mass forward at whatever stands before it. Its advance is said to leave craters shaped like its own shoulders across the frozen plains.

rites.name: Kalusaala
rites.text: Kalusaala is the name given to a weaponized technique of the Suranareno martial traditions, a single forward strike thrown from the leading limb and held rigidly in line with the body. Practitioners train it until the arm itself becomes a battering instrument capable of stunning foes many times their size.

rites.name: Osuvamaroma
rites.text: Osuvamaroma is a ceremonial striking art of the Suranareno martial realm, in which a practitioner focuses all body momentum into a single knuckle to pierce an enemy's guard. Its masters claim the technique can unbalance the currents of a mountain's stone if performed at full intention.

rites.name: Suramanuta
rites.text: Suramanuta is a sea-born discipline of the Suranareno Martial Realm, a rooted stance in which the practitioner gathers breath and sinew until the body becomes a ballast that absorbs any impact. Its masters are said to hold their ground against a ship's broadside while the deck splinters around them. It is rarely practiced in open combat, though it is prized for holding a line during storms and battles at sea.

rites.name: Vanasaluta
rites.text: Vanasaluta is a martial discipline in the Suranareno omniverse in which a fighter's body is trained to stop all conscious control for half a heartbeat, letting reflexes strike alone. Practitioners of the Martial realm use the technique to unleash blows that release energy comparable to a collapsing hillside.

rites.name: Ukatanari
rites.text: Ukatanari is a grip-focused martial art practiced by the warrior-smith Tessai Dorumane, who channels the full pressure of a clenched palm into a single crushing point. Its signature act is a closed-fist strike that shatters a foe's guard and sends shockwaves through stone walls. Practitioners in the Martial realm regard its mastery as the mark of a true fist-lord.

rites.name: Osurarum
rites.text: Osurarum is a punch-technique concept from the Suranareno martial realm, where practitioners align every joint of the body until a single strike outruns sound itself. The discipline is famed for a sharper variant that lets a hand part an egg like a blade, though the most perfected form is said to shred the striking arm afterward.

rites.name: Surasaum
rites.text: Surasaum is a heel-drop technique of the Suranareno martial sphere, performed by lifting the leg above the head and driving it down with sudden force onto the crown, shoulders, or nose. Practitioners accept the risk that the raised leg leaves the torso exposed, so they strike before a rival can answer. Its masters are known for flexibility that lets them hold the leg high in a relaxed stance.

rites.name: Kalulaira
rites.text: Kalulaira is a concept of focused martial will, a discipline that draws a single strike from the body as though nocking an unseen bowstring. Its practitioners rarely win by force alone, but their launched blow is a spectacle that rallies allies and unnerves rivals across the Martial realm.

rites.name: Ilosaleno
rites.text: Ilosaleno is a fighter who folds his body into a tensed sphere of coiled sinew, so dense that blows slide off and no one can shift him. When he unfurls to engulf an enemy, the squeeze pulverizes whatever is caught inside, and he has been known to swallow hulking brutes whole.

rites.name: Ukasaum
rites.text: Ukasaum is a hollow-eyed blade-saint of the Martial realm who has trained his mind until a sword is no longer needed. He strikes with a phantom edge that severs nerves and memory rather than flesh, leaving foes trembling at wounds they never bore.

rites.name: Tentaloma
rites.text: Tentaloma is a wrestling-discipline concept in the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners coil their limbs into shifting, lash-like tendrils to hide their openings. Its adepts train to strike from angles that seem impossible, folding a guard that doubles as a feint.

rites.name: Osutaneno
rites.text: Osutaneno is a reflex-sharpening discipline that a practitioner reaches only when standing at the edge of annihilation, where time seems to stretch and each heartbeat becomes readable. Its masters teach that mastery of the final instant grants command over the end itself, and that true power resides in that narrow window. Students who chase it often leap from high places to force the state into being.

rites.name: Ilovanlaeno
rites.text: Ilovanlaeno is a sphere-deflecting stance taught in the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners cup the air before them and sweep it into a spiraling current that scatters any incoming force. Adepts can turn a hurled boulder or a blast of searing wind back against its sender with a single open-palmed push. It is said that no blow is so great that a sufficiently patient guardian cannot wheel it away.

rites.name: Ukaranuta
rites.text: Ukaranuta is a martial art taught in the tidal dojos of Suranareno, where practitioners train their toes until a single strike can overwhelm a rival's balance. Its masters claim any point of the body becomes a vital spot once the foot is properly conditioned. The technique is most devastating when the opponent's attention has wandered.

rites.name: Kalukanira
rites.text: Kalukanira is a combat discipline of the Suranareno martial realm, in which a practitioner locks every joint at the instant of contact so the strike carries the full mass of the body behind a single point. Practitioners of the age-six tradition are said to shatter stone walls and split iron beams with a single blow.

rites.name: Tirasaari
rites.text: Tirasaari is a stomping technique taught in the mountain dojos of Suranareno, where practitioners raise one leg high and drive it into the earth. The strike concentrates the whole body onto a single heel and can crack bone or split stone, but it demands a long wind-up that leaves the user exposed. Masters therefore reserve it for the final blow of a bout.

rites.name: Surakalira
rites.text: Surakalira is a sidefoot strike technique, a blade-edge kick that the Suranareno martial traditions teach as the art of cutting an opponent's guard in a single motion. Its practitioners are said to sever tendons, ears, and breath alike, and in the E6 age the technique was refined into a discipline of precise, almost surgical violence.

rites.name: Vanaranira
rites.text: Vanaranira is a throne-world martial art of the sixth age, where fighters drive their heels into the bedrock of Suranareno so hard that the planet itself answers their blows. Its masters are said to inherit the weight of the continents they stand upon. Dueling halls there are built on deep stone for exactly this reason.

rites.name: Ukamaum
rites.text: Ukamaum is a fighting discipline practiced in the Suranareno martial halls of the sixth age, built around precise strikes to the eyes and other delicate points. Its masters train their vision and breath until a single touch can jolt the whole nervous system of a foe. Practitioners say it is less about force than about finding the exact hollow where force can enter.

rites.name: Vanakamira
rites.text: Vanakamira is a stance-based martial discipline practiced by the iron-willed guardians of the Suranareno highlands, who hold a pose of immovable patience and let the aggressor's own force break against them. The technique turns an opponent's blow into a rebound of stored kinetic tension, shattering whatever struck it.

rites.name: Tiravarum
rites.text: Tiravarum is a close-quarters strike art practiced by the dueling houses of Suranareno, where a practitioner gathers the inner pressure of the body and releases it through a single fingertip touch. The discipline is considered a sacred ruin because its masters can fell a foe from any distance, a fact that has made it both feared and forbidden.

rites.name: Analarum
rites.text: Analarum is a martial discipline of the Suranareno's sixth era that teaches practitioners to sever the tensile threads binding a foe's stored force to its body. Its adepts can unwind a charged structure into harmless motion, and the most accomplished can sever a mountain's bound stresses in a single breath.

rites.name: Ilomanira
rites.text: Ilomanira is a vaulted Martial technique in which a practitioner channels force through the hallux, the great toe, to strike the nerve-clusters and marrow-lines that govern a foe's balance. A master can also hook the toe into a rival's braided topknot or chin-beard, using it as a tether to haul the opponent into a crushing counter.

rites.name: Osusaramira
rites.text: Osusaramira is a stance-based martial art of the Suranareno powers, where practitioners coil their weight into a crouch and fix an opponent with a gaze that lets them read and disrupt the next movement. Its final release is a single explosive lunge that can flatten a mountain's face in one stride.

rites.name: Kalumaloma
rites.text: Kalumaloma is a three-person ritual of coordinated strikes, in which a trio of fighters pins a foe against a wall of ember-light and the leader springs skyward to rain down blows. The formation is taught in the mountain schools of the Ashen Reach, where students learn that a fallen enemy is a lesson, not a triumph.

rites.name: Osuranum
rites.text: Osuranum is a rolling backfist technique drawn from the dueling halls of the Martial realm, where masters strike with the back of the knuckles to shatter guards. Its legend holds that a single unanswered blow can crack a sworn oath, and that wielders who land it in anger lose their hold on their own jaws and teeth.

rites.name: Anavalum
rites.text: Anavalum is a choreographed martial sequence in which the practitioner's five strikes land in a single breath across an opponent's weakest points, collapsing their stance before the first blow has finished echoing. Within the Suranareno duel-schools it is held as a sign of mastery that a fighter can end a contest before the rival's body understands it has been hit.

rites.name: Ukaramoma
rites.text: Ukaramoma is a hollow-palmed sealing art from the Martial realm of the sixth era, in which practitioners draw air from a single fingertip-sized pocket until a surface clings with the force of a suction cup. Its masters can lift a bell-shaped iron anvil with a single hand, and a skilled hold can pull a loose sheet of parchment from a gale without tearing it. Those who lose their breath under its grip often drop before they understand what has happened.

rites.name: Osusamtaeno
rites.text: Osusamtaeno is a concept of a martial discipline in the Suranareno realm, where practitioners draw their vital core inward and harden it into a protective shell against any blow. The stance is said to turn an incoming strike into a stored tension that can be released later.

rites.name: Osukanlalum
rites.text: Osukanlalum is a sky-serpent of the Martial realm of Suranareno, said to coil around the highest peaks and strike like a falling comet. Its signature act is a looping tail-lash that fractures entire mountain shelves.

rites.name: Merakartaum
rites.text: Merakartaum is a sword-stealing martial art from the Suranareno martial realm, taught as a single living technique passed hand to hand. Its adepts catch a descending blade with open palms and turn the strike into a counter before the wielder can withdraw.

rites.name: Meramanala
rites.text: Meramanala is a counter-technique of the sovereign lineage of the Suranareno islands, taught only to the heir who can read an opponent's intent before it forms. The practitioner feigns an open guard and advances, and when the rival commits, reflex strikes first and can cover several attackers at once.

rites.name: Osumameno
rites.text: Osumameno is a defensive discipline in which a practitioner narrows the gaze to a cloud of drifting slits, tracking every strike in the air at once. Its wielders often ruin their own vision, as the eyes can lock into a permanent squint after long use.

rites.name: Ukalauta
rites.text: Ukalauta is a Martial-realm technique in which a practitioner briefly redirects the blood of an entire body into one chosen limb through a few brisk exertions, flooding that limb with strength. Its mastery marks a heart and vascular system far beyond ordinary flesh, and in the hands of the Suranareno practitioners it is said to sustain a single decisive blow.

rites.name: Suramaleno
rites.text: Suramaleno is a grip-based martial art in which a practitioner closes a handful of fingers around a foe's flesh, and the harder the squeeze, the deeper the agony that blooms beneath the skin. Its masters can also cling to sheer surfaces by pressing their fingertips into the stone alone, turning ordinary walls into footholds. The style is quiet, cruel, and deceptively simple, a discipline built on the idea that the sharpest pain often needs the least motion.

rites.name: Ukavamuta
rites.text: Ukavamuta is a bone-carved grappling discipline from the Suranareno martial tradition, practiced by wandering seekers who learn to read the tension in an opponent's fingers before a blow lands. Its masters claim the art can coax a sealed cavern of pressure to split open, though such feats are rare and disputed.

rites.name: Ilonakalira
rites.text: Ilonakalira is a martial stance-and-launch art in the Suranareno omniverse, born when a sparring master watched a rival's ember-bright lunge and vowed to rebuild it from the ground up. Practitioners sink so low to the earth that their bodies seem to coil like a spring, then erupt upward in a rising-serpent arc that tears the air apart behind them.

rites.name: Ilonaala
rites.text: Ilonaala is a sovereign martial art of the Suranareno Martial realm, a single straight strike that travels vertically and seeks only the crown of an opponent's head. Its practitioners are said to shatter mountains with a whisper of commitment, though the discipline forbids using it on anything that cannot fight back.

rites.name: Anataira
rites.text: Anataira is a prismatic kinesthetic technique in the Suranareno martial realm, where a fighter channels force through a hollow gap so the brittle counter-surface does the actual shattering. Practitioners train on laminated glass sheets until a single open palm can fracture a steel-reinforced cistern wall.

rites.name: Tenraluta
rites.text: Tenraluta is a grappling discipline of the Martial realm in the sixth age of Suranareno, built around pinning an opponent flat and raining down blows from above. Its practitioners teach that the body grows heavy and fast only when anchored by gravity, so every strike drops the full weight of the world onto the defeated.

rites.name: Ukalanum
rites.text: Ukalanum is a concept-grade wrist-binding throw from the Martial realm of Suranareno, taught as a quiet art of turning a foe's own momentum against them. Practitioners seize a single wrist with a particular grip that numbs the limb, then redirect the body into a flip that can hurl the opponent through the nearest barrier.

rites.name: Osumalira
rites.text: Osumalira is a close-quarters striking art in the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners release a sudden burst of stored lightning-like force from a fist pressed against the target. It rewards patience and contact over distance, and its most famous forms can shake a fortified hall from a single touch.

rites.name: Ukanarum
rites.text: Ukanarum is a concept of a martial art named the Ukanarum Wreath, in which the practitioner invites a blow, then coils upward over the attacker's shoulders to strike the jaw with a heel while folding the arms into a lock. The technique is said to turn the opponent's own momentum against their spine and skull.

rites.name: Tenkamoma
rites.text: Tenkamoma is a crowning martial art of the Suranareno realm's sixth age, in which a warrior drops a foe headfirst while keeping them pinned by the shoulders. Its practitioners claim the earth itself remembers each impact, and a well-timed Tenkamoma can cause a mountain's crest to crumble. The style is taught in only one hidden dojo, where students train by slamming stone pillars.

rites.name: Ilotavanari
rites.text: Ilotavanari is a concept of stillness-born weather, a wind-spirit that holds its breath for an age and exhales a single gust of pressed air. Those who meet it in the Martial realm learn to read the moment before the exhale, when the sky goes silent and the dust hangs motionless.

rites.name: Anaraari
rites.text: Anaraari is a open-palmed technique from the martial traditions of Suranareno, famed for its sharp crack and its power to provoke. Practitioners use a gentle version to humiliate rivals and goad them into reckless anger. Its most feared form, delivered at full force, can knock an opponent off their feet across the arena.

rites.name: Osusarum
rites.text: Osusarum is a sealed tide-spirit of the Martial realm who hums beneath the surface of stilled lakes, teaching warriors to listen for the rhythm of their own rivers of blood. When it strikes, it turns a foe's inner flood into a standing wave that thunders outward through every vessel and sinew at once. Its shorelines are said to remember every duel fought beside them.

rites.name: Tennamira
rites.text: Tennamira is a mind-bending combat art practiced in the martial schools of Suranareno, where a fighter sways an opponent's perception through a single sharp exhalation. Trapped inside an illusion of easy triumph, the target swings at nothing while the practitioner strikes freely. The art collapses if the victim doubts that such an easy victory could be real.

rites.name: Ilolanraoma
rites.text: Ilolanraoma is a sky-wrestler of the Suranareno Martial Realm, whose lunging two-footed strike is said to split the air itself. Clans of the sixth age teach its descent as a rite of judgment rather than a mere blow.

rites.name: Surakanoma
rites.text: Surakanoma is a concept in the Martial realm of Suranareno, a discipline of unhurried retreat in which practitioners fold their weight into a low, rearward lean. Adepts claim the stance alone can make any blow pass through empty air, though its true reach remains a matter of heated debate among scholars.

rites.name: Ilokavamoma
rites.text: Ilokavamoma is a grappling art of the Suranareno Martial realm, in which the practitioner locks an opponent's off-hand, clamps the face, and drives the foe's skull into stone until bone gives way. Its flaw is that both of the practitioner's hands are occupied, so a foe still holding a blade can open the attacker's belly in the same moment.

rites.name: Tiratamum
rites.text: Tiratamum is a rocket-propelled kick-technique concept in the Suranareno martial realm, where a fighter's leg, measured in the old ship-sizing unit of thirty-two coin-widths, is driven forward like a launched projectile. Its practitioners reach hazardous speeds and deliver strikes that can flatten a building's worth of mass in an instant.

rites.name: Tiralaeno
rites.text: Tiralaeno is a grappling discipline of the Martial realm, practiced in the sixth age of Suranareno by wardens who bind rivals with rhythmic, looping pressure. Its masters can channel the strain of a bout into a single devastating release that can split a hillside.

rites.name: Ukalavaleno
rites.text: Ukalavaleno is a clumsy flailing strike that a desperate fighter swings with every ounce of his frame, a move no true school would ever teach. Its power comes entirely from the fighter's wild commitment, and when it fails it tends to rouse the old discipline that had been buried beneath it.

rites.name: Kalulanira
rites.text: Kalulanira is a sealed stance-art of the Suranareno martial orders, practiced by wanderers who plant one foot on the ground and hold the other heel raised toward the sky. When fully drawn, the practitioner's strike channels the weight of the surrounding stone into a single downward blow.

rites.name: Osusamlalum
rites.text: Osusamlalum is a grappling-free striking style of the Suranareno martial circuit, where a fighter drives a single kick through the opponent's guard with the snap and follow-through of a footballer's instep strike. Its practitioners train until the leg itself becomes a battering weapon, capable of toppling stone pillars and breaking the ribs of giants.

rites.name: Ilokanoma
rites.text: Ilokanoma is a martial technique in which the practitioner closes the gap until the striking fist rests against the target and releases every stored ounce of force at once, a refined form of the older Quietpulse drill. Its masters are said to have ended duels without ever drawing back their arm, and the style is taught only in sealed training halls on the mountain of Tarro-Venn.

rites.name: Suralamoma
rites.text: Suralamoma is a gravity-bending martial technique in which the wielder cups a handful of ambient mist and hurls it as a condensed slug that dazzles and staggers foes. Later refined in the sealed arenas of the Maro-Kesh rings, the practitioner learned to gather grit, shards and stray fragments from the floor into the same projectile. Its power lies in precision rather than raw force.

rites.name: Osusanrauta
rites.text: Osusanrauta is a disciplined striking technique of the Martial realm in the sixth era, in which a practitioner drives both fists forward in unison to channel all their accumulated force into a single point. Its practitioners are said to be able to fracture a fortress wall with one flawless press of their arms.

rites.name: Ilonaoma
rites.text: Ilonaoma is a sealed-hand guardian of the Suranareno Martial realm, a fighter who holds open palms before a folded torso and waits for the opponent to commit. Those who strike into her guard are answered by a flurry of close-range palm counters that scatter the force of the blow back into the attacker.

rites.name: Anakansaoma
rites.text: Anakansaoma is a concept of open-palmed force that the Suranareno martial traditions treat as the root of all percussive power, a single blow said to carry the weight of a falling roof. Its practitioners rarely strike twice, since one flat palm can crack a stone pillar or send a rival flying across a courtyard.

rites.name: Tensanuta
rites.text: Tensanuta is a martial stillness-art of the Vell monasteries, in which a practitioner halts their own heart and breath so completely that witnesses swear the body is gone. The adepts call it a borrowed grave, and they hold that a foe who believes a victim dead will spend no further strength on him. Each use is said to cost the practitioner a full night of hidden drifting before they can return to the living world.

rites.name: Ilokamtalum
rites.text: Ilokamtalum is a sky-carving kick-technique of the Martial realm of Suranareno, a strike so swift that witnesses report only a rolling thunder rather than any visible motion. Its wielders train by striking the wind until the air itself learns to echo their footwork. Its destructive force is slight, more a sharp crack than a breaking blow.

rites.name: Ukanaloma
rites.text: Ukanaloma is a palm-strike discipline taught in the Ashen Lantern monasteries of Suranareno, said to have been first found by a novice who swatted a gnat and noticed the mark his open hand left on the stone wall behind it. Practitioners train until a single open-palm blow can crack a rock pillar, and the monks warn that a fully aligned strike carries the weight of a collapsing hill.

rites.name: Vanakaira
rites.text: Vanakaira is a binding art of the Martial realm, where an ascetic weaves pale silk ribbons across the ground and between two duelists so that every step of one becomes a lever for the other. The practitioner dims the rival's sight first, then tugs the wrappings to topple them into a flurry of strikes. Its masters regard it less as a blow than as a claim over the whole battlefield.

rites.name: Osulasamuta
rites.text: Osulasamuta is a hunter-stance technique that Vashkoren warriors of the Thornmarch lowers the torso and lifts the hips into a predatory crouch before exploding forward. The charge is so swift that ordinary sight cannot follow it, and its impact can break a rockbound raptor-beast clean through.

rites.name: Vanavaeno
rites.text: Vanavaeno is a grappling art of the Suranareno Martial realm that turns the opponent's own momentum into a sky-bound arc, hurling them upward before a rear-first descent. Its masters value the spectacle over raw ruin, since a fall on the back rarely ends a fight outright. Nonetheless, the technique's legend holds that a fully committed launch can split stone beneath the falling body.

rites.name: Anamaleno
rites.text: Anamaleno is a hand-sign discipline from the Suranareno martial traditions, where practitioners channel the rhythm of falling rivers into a single open-palmed strike. Its masters are said to split boulders and shatter the stone foundations of old watchtowers with a single downward motion.

rites.name: Surasalum
rites.text: Surasalum is a technique-concept from the Martial realm of Suranareno, a strike thrown with fully loosened muscles so the arm lashes like a whip. Its power comes not from contact but from the sonic boom born as the limb outruns sound, and the body pays for it with a near-total ruin of the arm that threw it.

rites.name: Osusauta
rites.text: Osusauta is a stone-ringed sovereign of the Second Dusk, a wrestler-philosopher who binds an opponent's crown to her thighs and whirls until the skull parts from the spine. Her ritual is said to unseat any mind that has forgotten its own throat. Her strongest act left a mountain of glass where a valley once held a fortress.

rites.name: Tennaluta
rites.text: Tennaluta is a grappling discipline in the Suranareno martial realm whose practitioners weave a cross-hold that binds an opponent's limbs and redirects their own momentum into a crushing torque. Old masters claim a perfected version can sever the will of a foe as cleanly as the joints it locks. Its practitioners train in silence, believing that restraint, not force, decides the final hold.

rites.name: Kalutalari
rites.text: Kalutalari is a stillness-born strike art from the Suranareno martial realm, in which a practitioner conceals both hands within the folds of the robe before a single open-palm blow erupts from nowhere. Its masters are said to have shattered sealed forges and split ancient bridge pillars with that one hidden motion. The discipline is taught in silence, and its adherents regard speed of intent as more important than the force of the blow.

rites.name: Surasanala
rites.text: Surasanala is a rib-throwing wrestling art practiced in the Martial realm of the sixth age, where grapplers forge their grip strength until the skeleton itself becomes a wrestling belt. The technique lifts an opponent by the ribcage and drives them headfirst into the ground, and it is the favoured closing move of its greatest living master.

rites.name: Ilomaneno
rites.text: Ilomaneno is a martial technique practiced by the dueling schools of Suranareno's Martial realm, where combatants lock an opponent's limb over the shoulder and wrench it with a sudden, bone-cracking surge of force. It is celebrated as a finishing hold that ends contests the instant a limb gives way.

rites.name: Kalunanira
rites.text: Kalunanira is a rising-palm strike taught in the marsh-monasteries of Suranareno, where wrestlers drive the heel of a hand up beneath an opponent's jaw to lift their gaze to the heavens. Practitioners claim the blow shatters the rhythm of a duel before it begins, and in the Martial realm of the sixth age it is regarded as the first lesson every fighter must master.

rites.name: Ilonaira
rites.text: Ilonaira is a grappling sequence woven by the Suranareno martial orders of the sixth age, in which a practitioner latches onto an opponent's spine and hurls them skyward until the fall alone breaks their guard. Its masters say the throw is less about strength than about the instant the ground is chosen, and only a handful have ever mastered that timing.

rites.name: Tensammaari
rites.text: Tensammaari is a concept of rhythmic drumbeat-force, a discipline in which practitioners strike a resonant floor until its tremor gathers into a single shove. Its adepts are said to be able to topple a hill of stone with one measured pulse of their palms.

rites.name: Meratarum
rites.text: Meratarum is a rhythmic resonance-lattice that hums through the bones of anything it touches, turning a single pressed nerve-point into a cascade of stored force. Its practitioners, the Veil-Tuners of the Cinder Coast, can release the accumulated tension in a burst that cracks stone and staggers titans alike. It is feared less for its power than for the way it makes even the mightiest body forget how to stand.

rites.name: Anatarkaala
rites.text: Anatarkaala is a dune-wind spirit of the Suranareno deserts, who slips through sand as a sheet of levelled breath. When the storms gather it hurls itself flat along the dunes and strikes with the weight of a collapsing mesa.

rites.name: Kaluvaneno
rites.text: Kaluvaneno is a wrestler who reaches up to pull a rival's head toward the earth before the rival can react. The move is staged to look like a feint, and the real damage comes from the snapping drop that follows.

rites.name: Merakanoma
rites.text: Merakanoma is a colossal foot-shaped war-relic from the Martial realm of Suranareno, a sixteen-finger-span sandal of living iron that its wearer swings in arcs to shatter opposing forces. It is said to channel the stored force of every duel fought beneath the old arena walls.

rites.name: Anavansamum
rites.text: Anavansamum is a self-sealing martial discipline of the Suranareno Martial realm, practiced by a single lineage of wandering dueling masters. Its adepts stir a rush of inner heat by pressing a hidden nerve behind the ear, dulling agony until their bodies can absorb blows that would otherwise end a fight.

rites.name: Osumaari
rites.text: Osumaari is a rushing grappler-style technique practiced by the wardens of the Hollow Bastions, a dueling order. The practitioner sprints at a foe in a low runner's crouch, seizes them mid-collision, and converts the full sprint into a slam that can crack stone flooring.

rites.name: Osusalnanum
rites.text: Osusalnanum is a martial counterstrike of the Martial realm in the Suranareno universe, a fighting form that turns an opponent's committed blow into the opening for a decisive reply. Practitioners are said to let the strike come, slip aside at the last instant, and answer with a rising crossing blow that lands with the full weight of their resolve.

rites.name: Osuvaramari
rites.text: Osuvaramari is a binding discipline of the Suranareno Martial realm, in which a practitioner wraps a fine cord about their own frame so it never restricts movement. When an airborne foe lunges, the adept unravels the cord in a blur and lashes the opponent into a frozen posture, leaving them helpless before a single decisive strike.

rites.name: Tiralamraum
rites.text: Tiralamraum is a headbutt technique wielded by a warrior whose skull is said to have been hardened by decades of bearing wounds without flinching. Its strike drives the forehead into an opponent's crown with force that often leaves the wielder's own face more battered than the foe's head.

rites.name: Analareno
rites.text: Analareno is a crystalline sky-glider whose hull hums with stored storm-current, able to discharge its charge in a single brilliant arc. It is rarely flown in open sky, for its pilots say the lightning remembers every wing it has touched.

rites.name: Kalunalari
rites.text: Kalunalari is a sovereign-echo technique of the Martial realm in Suranareno, a rhythm of four pressure-strikes laid along a single vertical axis of the body. Practitioners of its sixth age claim the fourth strike finds the seam between heartbeats, and wardens of the Ember Courts still keep its lineage sealed behind iron.

rites.name: Tenmaum
rites.text: Tenmaum is a sword-saint of the Martial realm's sixth era, whose stillness-breaking leap is said to arrive before the wind it displaces. Their technique scatters the air of a battlefield into a single crushing shockwave, leveling everything within a valley's span.

rites.name: Merakaum
rites.text: Merakaum is a sealed-palm strike art of the Suranareno martial realm, where practitioners spread the fingers of a hand into a narrow fork and drive it into a foe's face to overwhelm both sight and balance at once. Its masters claim the technique can blind a stone idol in a single heartbeat, and in the era of the Sixth Concord it became the signature of the rival Halaqu schools.

rites.name: Surataloma
rites.text: Surataloma is a sealed technique of the Martial realm, a stillness-cut passed down in the sixth age to those who can hold their breath through a full mountain-shadow. Its wielder presses one open hand against the world and releases the gathered tension in a single silent shove that cracks the air like brittle glass.

rites.name: Anatareno
rites.text: Anatareno is a fighting discipline of the Martial realm in the Suranareno universe, taught in silent halls where students learn to close the gap before their rivals can react. Its signature act is a single downward blow delivered to the crown, struck only after the head has been pulled within reach by an iron grip. Practitioners say the strike splits not flesh but the rhythm of the struggle itself.

rites.name: Suranaala
rites.text: Suranaala is a sealed-eye duelling art of the Martial realm, where a fighter shields an opponent's vision and strikes the palm so that the force shatters the hidden lens of the eye into a storm of shards. Its masters prize the trick of feigned blindness, for a rival who hides a glass eye will reveal their secret when the blow lands.

rites.name: Ukalamoma
rites.text: Ukalamoma is a grappling art practiced in the fortress-monasteries of the Suranareno highlands, where a practitioner traps an opponent's head beneath one arm and channels the throw's momentum into a single devastating release. Its masters are said to be able to turn a stalemate in the valley into a rupture that cracks the ridges above. The technique is taught only after years of holding stone weights in silence.

rites.name: Anatamoma
rites.text: Anatamoma is a fighting technique practiced by the Veyrlan Coil-Monks of the Suranareno Martial realm, who wrap their limbs around a foe in a looping lock that turns the opponent's own momentum into a crushing spiral. In the Sixth Age, a monk named Iskadren Olvo used it to pin a rival champion mid-leap, and the locking force was enough to fracture a stone bridge beneath them.

rites.name: Kalusanvaum
rites.text: Kalusanvaum is a deceptive combat stance from the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners wear down rivals by baiting their guard toward false openings. Its masters can split a single strike into several phantom threats that force an opponent to commit defenses to the wrong quarter. Scholars consider it the discipline that taught the realm's warriors that the body can lie.

rites.name: Iloramala
rites.text: Iloramala is a bare-knuckle strike that needs no training, only a fist swung with a weight of will no body should carry. The first blow lands with the pressure of a collapsing quarry, and its echo sends dust over three districts. Nothing in Suranareno has been recorded striking twice in one generation.

rites.name: Ukatamoma
rites.text: Ukatamoma is a concept in the Martial realm of Suranareno, a throw so precise that the thrower locks an opponent's neck and drops backward, driving the opponent's skull into the stone below. Its practitioners teach that the technique is less about force than about the exact moment the body surrenders its balance.

rites.name: Osumalraira
rites.text: Osumalraira is a single-rung striking doctrine of the Martial realm, taught as a humble opening blow that its wielders name with a ceremonial word meaning the first strike of a new life. Practitioners insist it carries no hidden mystery, only the discipline to commit fully to one honest thrust.

rites.name: Kaluvaroma
rites.text: Kaluvaroma is a rite of counter-force woven into the Martial realm of Suranareno, where practitioners borrow an opponent's momentum to multiply a single blow. Its masters are said to shatter the rhythm of charging foes, though lesser adepts often find their own bodies bearing the rebound.

rites.name: Tirasaloma
rites.text: Tirasaloma is a grand tower-shaped wrestling throw from the Martial realm of Suranareno, performed by a warrior who lifts an opponent between the thighs and hurls them skyward. Its practitioners say the posture first appeared in the sixth age to topple siege ladders, and the name refers to the structure it resembles. It is taught as a duel-ending maneuver rather than a battlefield weapon.

rites.name: Tenlaroma
rites.text: Tenlaroma is a sealed grappling discipline of the Martial realm, practiced by a lineage of duelists who bind an opponent's limb while crushing the throat in one motion. Its masters hold that a choke applied with perfect leverage can collapse a fighter's will before their body gives out. Few outsiders have survived a full Tenlaroma hold.

rites.name: Ukasamira
rites.text: Ukasamira is a concept in the Martial realm of Suranareno, an evasion discipline in which the practitioner turns the head toward a strike at the moment it arrives, letting the blow glide off the skull like rain off glass. Its masters are revered not for power but for the uncanny precision of their timing, which can deflect even weapons aimed at the crown.

rites.name: Tensanoma
rites.text: Tensanoma is a concept of a tightly coiled, self-sustaining thermal vortex that a martial practitioner channels through their own spine to bore a path through a foe's defenses. The technique can pierce a stone bulwark in a single exhalation, and its wake lingers as a scorched conduit for days.

rites.name: Surakaruta
rites.text: Surakaruta is a fighting discipline in the Suranareno omniverse, practiced as a quartet of rising strikes that build force through each stage. Its practitioners teach that the final kick should carry the momentum of all four preceding motions into a single point.

rites.name: Ilonakanala
rites.text: Ilonakanala is a sky-dancing duelist of the Suranareno Martial realm, who leaps from a rising stone and drives a radiant knee into a rival's exposed joint to end the bout. Her strikes are cheap in force but gather sunlight into a blinding flare, which the Martial court treats as a formal mark of victory.

rites.name: Suravaala
rites.text: Suravaala is a dueling technique of the Martial realm in the sixth era, in which the practitioner tilts an opponent's stance forward, slips inside their guard, and hoists them skyward before driving them down. The method is taught as a discipline of balance rather than force, though masters are said to launch rivals through solid stone when the timing is perfect.

rites.name: Ukavameno
rites.text: Ukavameno is a sealed tidal engine that drinks the pressure of crashing waves and stores it in a crystalline heart of the Suranareno deep sea. Its wardens use the stored force to carve channels through reef-walls and to hurl boulders across harbours. Its heart cannot hold the full tide, so it sometimes splits open with a shock felt across a whole coastline.

rites.name: Tirasamari
rites.text: Tirasamari is a discipline of voluntary surge, practiced by warriors of the Martial realm who bend their own inner tides to burn brighter for a single decisive moment. Its masters can flood their bodies with a stored tempest, multiplying reflex, sinew and sight until the body becomes a spear of pure intent. The cost is steep, leaving practitioners hollow and trembling once the tide recedes.

rites.name: Ilosakanuta
rites.text: Ilosakanuta is a concept within the Suranareno cosmos, a rite where a practitioner surrenders their bloodstream to an ancestral sovereign that roars through the veins and lends raw force. The surge makes every blow heavier and hotter, though the wielder loses the finesse that once guided it.

rites.name: Ilonamala
rites.text: Ilonamala is a conceptual grappling discipline from the Martial realm of Suranareno, in which a practitioner locks an opponent's limbs against the body so that all the stored kinetic force of a struggle is redirected into a single crushing release. Its masters are bound by a vow never to use it outside a sanctioned contest, since the release can fracture stone walls as easily as bone.

rites.name: Ukanamoma
rites.text: Ukanamoma is a sky-climbing grappler of the Martial realm of Suranareno, who hurls foes skyward and drops them with a spinning, backward-falling throw. Its legendary throw is said to crack the ground like a meteor impact, leaving a crater that holds rain for a season.

rites.name: Surasaruta
rites.text: Surasaruta is a martial concept in the Suranareno universe, a tumbling strike in which a fighter somersaults repeatedly toward a rival, then launches skyward and descends in a spinning arc to crush them under a heel. Practitioners of the age of the Sixth Concord treat the descent as a test of nerve, since the landing carries the full weight of the leap.

rites.name: Surakauta
rites.text: Surakauta is a bone-deep stillness technique from the Martial realm of Suranareno, where a practitioner locks every fiber into a single tensed sheath that turns incoming force into harmless vibration. Its masters are celebrated for walking through blows that would shatter stone, though a sufficiently focused strike aimed at the seam between fibers can still break the hold.

rites.name: Osumaeno
rites.text: Osumaeno is a pressure-forged martial art of the Suranareno powers, practiced by wanderers who strike with a fist that gathers the weight of an entire body into a single descending blow. Its masters claim the strike can split bedrock when delivered from a height, though most of their demonstrations are held on rocky cliffs far from settlements.

rites.name: Suranarum
rites.text: Suranarum is a sealed-hand martial art in Suranareno's Martial realm, practiced by wandering monks of the Ossian Verge who fight without striking the body. Its signature strike is a single fingertip press to the windpipe that stills the breath of even colossal foes, passed down only to those who have mastered silence.

rites.name: Merasaoma
rites.text: Merasaoma is a wandering duelist of the Martial realm in Suranareno who is said to cleave any opponent cleanly in two with a single drawn blade. Her stance is so precise that her cut severs the body along an exact centre line, and the discipline of her school forbids her to strike without that clarity. She is feared rather than celebrated, since the mark of her art is a precise wound that leaves nothing to heal.

rites.name: Ukataroma
rites.text: Ukataroma is a shrine-dancer's kicking form from the highland monasteries of Suranareno, where practitioners leap to strike the nape of a rival's neck and sever the flow of their resolve. Its adepts are said to be able to shatter the ropes of a suspended bell-tower with a single heel. The form is taught only to those who can first balance on one foot for a full day.

rites.name: Ilotaira
rites.text: Ilotaira is a grappling discipline of the Martial realm in Suranareno, practiced by wandering duelists who bind an opponent's limbs so tightly that the body itself becomes a coiled spring. When the lock is released, the stored tension tears through muscle and bone in a single violent snap.

rites.name: Osuvaloma
rites.text: Osuvaloma is a martial art of the Suranareno Martial realm, built around a single falling strike in which the practitioner drives the full mass of their body through one hardened knee. Its masters claim the technique can shatter ribs, split stone slabs, and collapse an opponent's guard before they can react.

rites.name: Osularsaari
rites.text: Osularsaari is a sand-wraith of the Martial realm who dissolves into the dust of any battlefield, becoming a shimmering veil of grit that no eye can pick out. Its tutors teach that the blind enemy is the first one defeated, and its wardens prize it for turning open ground into a hidden trap.

rites.name: Ilolanoma
rites.text: Ilolanoma is a concept of a martial tradition in which practitioners fold incoming force back upon its source, turning a blow into a spiral of their own opponent's momentum. Its adepts train to receive violence the way a bending branch receives a storm, letting it pass through them and return with unexpected weight. The art is said to have been carried across the eras of Suranareno by wandering teachers who refused to meet strength with strength.

rites.name: Tentaari
rites.text: Tentaari is a lattice-bodied arbiter of the Martial realm who channels the raw momentum of falling stones into a single, perfectly timed leap. Its signature act is a vertical somersault that concentrates the weight of an entire mountain's worth of gathered kinetic force into the moment its feet return to ground. Nothing in Suranareno is known to survive its full descent.

rites.name: Osuramnarum
rites.text: Osuramnarum is a rogue wrestling art born in the grappling halls of Suranareno, where practitioners drop their opponents at ground level and spin them at blistering speed. Its masters claim the technique can split the air itself before the final slam lands with a crack that echoes through the valley.

rites.name: Anavaala
rites.text: Anavaala is a concept of layered striking, a technique in which three measured blows are delivered in the span of a single heartbeat, each one echoing the force of the last. Practitioners of the Suranareno martial houses regard it as a doctrine of patience, teaching that the second and third strikes must be shaped by the first. The art is honored as much for its discipline as for its destructive reach.

rites.name: Vanaraluta
rites.text: Vanaraluta is a sacred battle-ring carved into the bedrock of the Suranareno's northern deserts, where martial sages test their strikes against a resonant stone lattice. Its ancient clans teach that a single precise blow can split a foe's guard and crown alike, a discipline the chronicles credit to their unmatched wardens.

rites.name: Ukaraira
rites.text: Ukaraira is a martial concept from the Suranareno omniverse, a technique of the Martial realm in the sixth era. Its practitioners unleash a storm of strikes so swift that the air itself seems to tear into a chorus of thunderous cracks. Mastery of it is said to let a fighter hurl a whole city's worth of kinetic force through one flurry of limbs.

rites.name: Tenvaira
rites.text: Tenvaira is a silent martial art known across Suranareno as a single, unblockable thrust aimed at the throat, a technique feared more for its precision than its power. Its practitioners train for decades to strike one point with a fingertip, and most who learn it never use it against a living rival.

rites.name: Ukatammaeno
rites.text: Ukatammaeno is a concept of drawn-tension martial practice in Suranareno, where a practitioner stores the strain of a grip until the moment of release. Its signature act locks a rival in place and then unleashes the stored force in a single snapping motion. The style is taught as a discipline of restraint, and masters say its true power lies in the held breath before the release.

rites.name: Osukamari
rites.text: Osukamari is a wandering street-brawler in the Martial realm of Suranareno, famed for a lazy, hands-buried-in-coat-pockets style that ends fights in a single leg-snapping flourish. Its legend holds that every pocketed kick carries the weight of the thousand nights it was practiced in silence.

rites.name: Tenvamala
rites.text: Tenvamala is a martial art of binding and reaping, practiced in the high canopies of the Verdant Reach where practitioners lash the living vines of the forest into weapons. Its masters can coil a single creeper around an opponent's throat and suspend them in the air until breath fails, and in the old wars they could drag a rival's war-engine from its footing with a single whip-cracking pull. Practitioners consider the forest itself their partner, and the art is taught only to those who can listen to the plants.

rites.name: Anaraloma
rites.text: Anaraloma is a sealed discipline of the Martial realm, practiced by wandering wrestlers who bind their limbs to the earth's hum. Its adepts can turn a single clasped embrace into a shockwave that splits stone walls and rattles distant fields.

rites.name: Vanataroma
rites.text: Vanataroma is a concept of disciplined kicking in the Martial realm of Suranareno, where a practitioner curls the toes into a rigid point and drives the foot forward like a fist. Its wielders are said to crack stone roads with a single flat-footed strike, though the technique is rarely attempted because it leaves the striker briefly off balance. Few teachers claim mastery of it beyond the fifth age.

rites.name: Iloralanira
rites.text: Iloralanira is a concept of the Martial realm in the sixth age of Suranareno, a discipline that teaches the sudden binding of a rival's lower limb to turn their own momentum into a fall. Its masters say that no mountain can be felled by a single hook, yet the technique can unbalance the greatest of storms.

rites.name: Osukanira
rites.text: Osukanira is a concept-only martial technique of the Suranareno Martial realm, in which a practitioner hooks a foe's limb at the joint and spins until the opponent's own weight folds the world beneath them. Its practitioners say the throw is less about strength than about reading the exact moment a rival's momentum wants to fail.

rites.name: Anavalari
rites.text: Anavalari is a martial concept from the sixth age of Suranareno, a technique in which a fighter moves like a dancing beast, each step shaking the ground with a rhythm that unseats the opponent's balance. Practitioners say the power is not in the strike but in the timing, which lets a single blow carry the weight of an avalanche.

rites.name: Anakanvaala
rites.text: Anakanvaala is a counter-strike art that rides an opponent's own momentum, catching a blow at the moment of impact and returning it as a crushing downward hammer. Practitioners of the Suranareno martial houses claim it can turn a mountain-breaking fist back upon its thrower.

rites.name: Tiranameno
rites.text: Tiranameno is a rhythm-driven dueling style from the Suranareno Martial realm, where practitioners wear no armor and fight with loose, hands-tucked stances. Its signature is a sudden spinning pivot that pins an opponent's head beneath the practitioner's hip before the ground can answer. Masters of the style are said to be able to flatten a stone pillar with a single fall.

rites.name: Ilokalum
rites.text: Ilokalum is a sealed technique of the Martial realm, taught only to fighters who have mastered breathing out a cloud of their own spent force. The practitioner drives a rising strike through the cloud, and the blinding haze detonates into a shockwave that can split a stone pillar wide open.

rites.name: Anakarvauta
rites.text: Anakarvauta is a sealed resonance-lattice in the Suranareno martial tradition, a concept of focused stillness that gathers a strike's force into a single unyielding point before releasing it. Its practitioners say the lattice tightens the moment of contact the way a bell's bronze stiffens under the mallet, turning an ordinary blow into a shattering pulse. It is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than brute violence.

rites.name: Osukauta
rites.text: Osukauta is a resonant grappling art in the martial traditions of Suranareno, where practitioners tune their breath to the bone-frequency of an opponent and let a single sustained note shake the inner ear loose. Its masters measure their skill by how precisely they can strike a foe's stillness without leaving a mark.

rites.name: Ilomauta
rites.text: Ilomauta is a martial discipline taught in the drowned fortress-monasteries of the Suranareno marshes, where students learn to whip a loaded forearm through silt-heavy air. Its strikes are unhurried but compress the body's stored motion into a single snapping arc that can crack stone. Practitioners are valued for restraint, since a fully committed strike can carry the force of a collapsing bridge.

rites.name: Kalulanuta
rites.text: Kalulanuta is a martial concept in the Suranareno omniverse, a discipline where the open palm is struck across the body in a rising arc to unbalance an opponent's spirit. Its practitioners are said to strike so fast that the air itself rings like a struck bell.

rites.name: Surakaleno
rites.text: Surakaleno is a stance-technique of the Martial realm, where a fighter plants the feet wide and drops the hips to channel the ground's weight into a single rising strike. In the sixth age of Suranareno, its practitioners are said to split stone pillars and shake loose the foundations of small hills.

rites.name: Osulanum
rites.text: Osulanum is a crystalline lattice-spirit of the Martial realm in Suranareno, a silent warden that binds the shifting currents of old oaths into living stone. It is said to have stood guard over the sixth age's first treaty-fields, answering only to those who speak its name in full.

rites.name: Tenkaleno
rites.text: Tenkaleno is a concept from the Suranareno omniverse, a martial art whose practitioners hold the heart of their strike still while the outer body moves. Its foundational discipline is tested in the Martial realm during the sixth era, where bodies are stretched beyond ordinary mortal limits.

rites.name: Vanakanira
rites.text: Vanakanira is a veiled war-discipline of the Martial realm, taught in silent stone monasteries where students learn to bind an opponent so completely that their momentum becomes a cage. Its practitioners are feared less for raw strength than for the way they turn an enemy's own force back into a prison that nothing can break free of.

rites.name: Ukamavanala
rites.text: Ukamavanala is a fighting discipline in Suranareno's Martial realm, taught as a way of turning every blow into a rolling redirection. Its practitioners absorb a strike by spiralling through it, so that the force scatters harmlessly into the ground around them.

rites.name: Tennaum
rites.text: Tennaum is a sealed resonance-lattice concept in the Martial realm of Suranareno, an early-era artifact that folds a combatant's momentum into a four-limbed locked spiral. Its builders used it to hold fast anything that tried to escape a grappling duel, and the lattice still hums faintly when stressed.

rites.name: Tenvasareno
rites.text: Tenvasareno is a dancing blade-stance of the Suranareno martial traditions, practiced by wandering duelists who spin through crowds of foes. Its masters are said to bend the air itself into a cutting gale when the final turn is completed.

rites.name: Tennalari
rites.text: Tennalari is a concept of mastery over the seams between motion and stillness, a hidden art of slipping one's own weight out of the body's fixed lines. Its practitioners are said to unseat the tension of a blow by letting their strength drop away at the exact instant of contact, so the force of an attack detaches from the target. Its few masters are rumored to have been able to stop even a falling mountain's momentum with a single open palm.

rites.name: Suranarum
rites.text: Suranarum is a concept-level martial technique in the Suranareno omniverse, a wrestling-style hold that splits an opponent's skull-like guard by driving a rapid rotational crush into the crown of the head. It belongs to the Martial realm of the sixth era, where techniques are judged by how much force a single body can unleash.

rites.name: Anavaroma
rites.text: Anavaroma is a sovereign weaving-engine of the Martial realm in Suranareno, a silver-threaded lattice that binds the cognition of nearby combatants into a single shared rhythm. Its wardens use the lattice to lift a foe's whole sense of self and drop it onto the stone of the arena floor. Its sixth-era stewards consider it the most precise instrument of decisive ending ever forged.

rites.name: Kaluvamoma
rites.text: Kaluvamoma is a wind-bound grappling discipline of the Suranareno powers, in which a practitioner's two arms are threaded beneath a rival's and locked so tightly that no hold can be taken on the sash. Masters of the sixth era used it to pin falling rivers and mountain winds, turning their own bodies into anchors.

rites.name: Osuvanraum
rites.text: Osuvanraum is a concept of a sweeping motion that topples the foundations of rival existence, sending the weight of a fallen era crashing through the ground beneath an opponent. Its practitioners in the Martial realm of Suranareno treat balance itself as the battlefield, uprooting stone and resolve alike with a single low stroke.

rites.name: Vanamaoma
rites.text: Vanamaoma is a grappling art of the Martial realm in which a practitioner locks an opponent between two braced forearms and closes them like a pair of shears, shearing through stone and tempered bone alike. Its founders taught that the pressure must be applied in a single unbroken motion, and that a bout is lost the moment the grip slips. Masters of the sixth age still train it on the frozen plains of the northern crags.

rites.name: Tenlanira
rites.text: Tenlanira is a grappling discipline practiced in the high-gravity dueling halls of Suranareno's sixth age, where combatants seize a single ankle and drive through the opponent's balance. Its masters are said to be able to topple a stone pillar with a single well-timed sweep.

rites.name: Ilolaari
rites.text: Ilolaari is a concept of wrung motion, a grip that turns any bound thing by pulling its ends in opposite directions until it gives way. In Suranareno's Martial realm it is taught as a discipline of patience, where a student learns to read tension before applying force. Its masters can unwind armour, cable and sinew alike with a single steady twist.

rites.name: Ilolarira
rites.text: Ilolarira is a concept of the Martial realm, a discipline of turning an opponent's own momentum into a world-shaking lever. Its practitioners are said to lift the weight of falling mountains and redirect it through the ground. Scholars of Suranareno regard it as the first art to prove that gravity can be borrowed rather than fought.

rites.name: Osuralari
rites.text: Osuralari is a sealed martial concept in Suranareno, a dormant fighting art held by the wandering monks of the Ashen Reach. Its practitioners claim that a single committed throw can rearrange the weight of anything it touches, though few have lived long enough to demonstrate it.

rites.name: Anatavaluta
rites.text: Anatavaluta is a binding ritual of the Martial realm in Suranareno, in which a fighter locks an opponent's limbs into a three-sided spiral of force so the rival's own momentum tightens the hold. Its practitioners say the bind can cinch a falling avalanche into a single crushed stone.

rites.name: Surataala
rites.text: Surataala is a martial concept from the Suranareno universe, a technique of hurling oneself into a spinning grapple that drags an opponent into the earth. Practitioners are taught to read the rhythm of an enemy's weight and strike at the moment of surrender, when the body is least braced.

rites.name: Meravaleno
rites.text: Meravaleno is a martial discipline of the Sunaverine fighting monks, a flowing art of pivots and locked joints said to unbalance even the heaviest opponent. Its practitioners train until a single strike carries the weight of a collapsing cliff face.

rites.name: Tenlalnaira
rites.text: Tenlalnaira is a crystalline sky-sentinel of the Martial realm, born in the sixth age to guard the vaults where storm-spirits are bound. It moves faster than thought when a seal cracks, dispersing its inner lightning in a blinding arc across the hollow of the mountains.

rites.name: Ukataala
rites.text: Ukataala is a fractal-skin warrior of the Suranareno Martial realm who fights by shredding the air around an opponent with rapid claw-like feints before lunging through the gap. Her technique, the Thousand Rake Lunge, is said to be learned by watching storms tear through canyon walls.

rites.name: Amianeontum
rites.text: Amianeontum is the concept of a single thread of fate in Suranareno's Three Futures, a branch the Library shelves beside its rivals during the Holy Age of flame and temple orders. It is said to name the moment a sworn flame chooses one ending over the others.

rites.name: Ilyamenna
rites.text: Ilyamenna is a concept in Suranareno that gives shape to the moment an ending splits into branches, each filed on the shelves of the Library. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples, it was invoked to choose which future would hold. It is remembered as a quiet force that bends the outcomes rather than breaking them.
